title: Make auto-backup exclusion explicit
findings_note: res/xml/backup_rules.xml and res/xml/data_extraction_rules.xml (template files with TODOs); AndroidManifest.xml (allowBackup=false)
boundary: **Not in this slice:** enabling any form of Android backup or device transfer. The owner decided it stays disabled.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: The manifest sets `allowBackup="false"` but still points at the Android Studio template rule files, which are comments and a TODO. The behaviour is correct, but it relies on a single flag and the files look unfinished. Explicit rules make the intent deterministic and lint-clean.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. `backup_rules.xml`:
   ```xml
   <?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
   <full-backup-content>
       <exclude domain="root" path="." />
       <exclude domain="file" path="." />
       <exclude domain="database" path="." />
       <exclude domain="sharedpref" path="." />
       <exclude domain="external" path="." />
   </full-backup-content>
   ```
2. `data_extraction_rules.xml`: put the same five `<exclude>` lines inside both `<cloud-backup>` and `<device-transfer>`.
3. Keep `allowBackup="false"` and both attributes in the manifest.
4. `PRIVACY.md` already says automatic Android backup is disabled, so it needs no change.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `./gradlew lintDebug` reports no new warnings, and none about backup or data extraction rules.
- `./gradlew assembleDebug` passes and the app launches.
